labs.title: Govern AI models and agents through an API gateway
labs.description: Deploy the Citadel AI Governance Hub, then govern every model, access contract, and agent through a single API Management gateway: onboard backends, enforce model RBAC and quotas, observe usage and cost, mask PII, and publish governed agents and MCP tools. A modular lab you can complete end to end or one task at a time.

extra.concepts: AI governance, API Management gateway, access contracts, observability, PII protection, agent governance

labs.title: Getting started: deploy the Citadel governance hub
labs.description: Shared setup for the Govern AI models and agents lab: register resource providers, deploy the Citadel hub and a sample spoke with azd, and set up your Python environment. Complete this once before any task.

extra.concepts: environment setup, azd deployment, hub-and-spoke

labs.title: Task 1 – Onboard AI backends and call the Universal LLM API
labs.description: Register AI model backends with the Citadel API Management gateway and route every model call through the Universal LLM API, using the workshop onboarding and validation notebooks.

extra.concepts: API Management gateway, backend onboarding, Universal LLM API, model routing

labs.title: Task 2 – Enforce access contracts with model RBAC and quotas
labs.description: Deploy Citadel access contracts that pin each workload to specific models (model-level RBAC) and cap its token spend with per-minute and quota limits, then validate the enforcement and throttling behavior.

extra.concepts: access contracts, model RBAC, token quotas, rate limiting, APIM products and subscriptions

labs.title: Task 3 – Observe usage, cost, and throttling
labs.description: Explore the telemetry your governed gateway generates: API Management Analytics and metrics, KQL log queries, Application Insights traces, and token-level usage records in Cosmos DB enriched with model pricing.

extra.concepts: observability, APIM analytics, KQL, Application Insights, Cosmos DB usage records, cost analytics

labs.title: Task 4 – Protect sensitive data with PII policies
labs.description: Add gateway policies that anonymize and de-anonymize, or outright block, personally identifiable information in prompts, then analyze PII processing records from Cosmos DB.

extra.concepts: PII detection, anonymization, data protection policies, Azure AI Language, access contracts

labs.title: Task 5 – Govern agent frameworks and the Unified AI API
labs.description: Route three different agent frameworks (Microsoft Agent Framework, Foundry SDK, LangChain) through their access contracts, then validate the multi-provider Unified AI API surface with its path rules, model access control, and debug headers.

extra.concepts: agent frameworks, Unified AI API, multi-provider routing, model access control, gateway policies

labs.title: Task 6 – Publish and govern a hosted agent and an A2A endpoint
labs.description: Build, deploy, and govern a Foundry hosted agent with the Agent Governance Toolkit, then publish a Foundry agent through API Management as a governed Agent-to-Agent (A2A) endpoint callable with only a subscription key.

extra.concepts: hosted agents, Agent Governance Toolkit, agent policy enforcement, Agent-to-Agent (A2A), access contracts

labs.title: Task 7 – Publish and govern an HR MCP server through APIM
labs.description: Deploy an HR Model Context Protocol server, publish it through API Management as a governed access contract with a tool-call rate limit, and consume its tools from a Microsoft Agent Framework agent — all through the gateway.

extra.concepts: Model Context Protocol (MCP), MCP governance, rate limiting, access contracts, Microsoft Agent Framework

labs.title: Build and extend AI agents
labs.description: Build the Caldova supply chain assistant: ground it in company policy, then extend it with tools using remote MCP servers, custom functions, and a client app. A modular lab you can complete end to end or one task at a time.

extra.concepts: agent creation and grounding, tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP)

labs.title: Getting started: set up your environment
labs.description: Shared setup for the Build and extend AI agents lab: create a Microsoft Foundry project, get the starter code, and configure your environment. Complete this once before any task.

extra.concepts: environment setup, Microsoft Foundry project

labs.title: Task 1 – Create and ground an agent
labs.description: Create an agent in the Microsoft Foundry portal and ground it in Caldova supply chain policy so it answers from your data.

extra.concepts: agent creation, grounding, file search

labs.title: Task 2 – Connect a remote MCP server
labs.description: Extend an agent with a tool by connecting it to a remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, and handle tool-approval requests in code.

extra.concepts: tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP), approvals

labs.title: Task 3 – Call your agent from a client app
labs.description: Drive your grounded portal agent from a small web chat app using the Foundry SDK and Responses API, with inline charts.

extra.concepts: Foundry SDK, Responses API, code interpreter

labs.title: Task 4 – Add custom function tools
labs.description: Give an agent tools backed by your own Python functions and process the function-calling loop.

extra.concepts: function tools, function calling, Microsoft Agent Framework

labs.title: Task 5 – Capstone: build your own MCP server
labs.description: Capstone: build your own MCP server and combine it with your function tools into one Caldova assistant.

extra.concepts: MCP server, tool orchestration, Microsoft Agent Framework

labs.title: Task 6 – Promote your assistant to a hosted agent
labs.description: Take the Caldova assistant you built as a prompt agent and deploy it as a hosted agent - your own code running in a Foundry-managed container - with the Azure Developer CLI.

extra.concepts: hosted agents, deployment, Azure Developer CLI

labs.title: Integrate agents with enterprise knowledge and Microsoft 365
labs.description: Build the Caldova staff knowledge assistant: ground it on enterprise documents with Foundry IQ, then deliver it through Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Copilot, and Work IQ. A modular lab you can complete end to end or one task at a time.

extra.concepts: enterprise knowledge grounding, Foundry IQ, Microsoft 365, Model Context Protocol (MCP)

labs.title: Getting started: set up your environment
labs.description: Shared setup for the Integrate agents with enterprise knowledge and Microsoft 365 lab: create a Microsoft Foundry project, get the starter code, and configure your environment. Complete this once before any task.

extra.concepts: environment setup, Microsoft Foundry project

labs.title: Task 1 – Create a Foundry IQ knowledge agent and connect from code
labs.description: Create an enterprise-knowledge agent in the Microsoft Foundry portal, ground it on the Caldova knowledge base with Foundry IQ, require approval before knowledge lookups, then connect from code and handle the approval flow.

extra.concepts: Foundry IQ, enterprise knowledge grounding, tool approvals, conversations API

labs.title: Task 2 – Publish your agent to Microsoft Teams
labs.description: Publish the Caldova knowledge agent to Microsoft Teams so staff can chat with it where they already work.

extra.requires: A Microsoft 365 account with Teams access, and permission to publish agents to Teams in your tenant
extra.verify: In the Foundry portal, open your agent and select **Publish**. If Teams is greyed out or returns a consent error, you don't have the rights this task needs.
extra.concepts: agent publishing, Microsoft Teams, Azure Bot Service

labs.title: Task 3 – Publish your agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot
labs.description: Publish the Caldova knowledge agent to Microsoft 365 Copilot so staff can reach it inside Copilot.

extra.requires: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, and permission to publish agents to Copilot in your tenant
extra.verify: In the Foundry portal, open your agent and select **Publish**. If Microsoft 365 Copilot is greyed out or returns a consent error, you don't have the rights this task needs.
extra.concepts: agent publishing, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot agents

labs.title: Task 4 – Work IQ: bring Microsoft 365 signals into an agent
labs.description: Build an agent that accesses Microsoft 365 workplace data using Work IQ and the Model Context Protocol for meeting prep, project tracking, and action items.

extra.requires: A Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, IT admin consent for Work IQ, and Node.js 18 or later
extra.verify: Run the command below. If it returns your calendar you're ready; if it reports missing consent or no Copilot licence, skip this task.
extra.verify_command: npm install -g @microsoft/workiq && workiq accept-eula && workiq ask -q "What meetings do I have today?"
extra.concepts: Work IQ, Microsoft 365, Model Context Protocol (MCP), function tools

labs.title: Build multi-agent solutions with the Agent Framework
labs.description: Build Caldova operations agents with the Microsoft Agent Framework: start with a single tool-using agent, then orchestrate several agents in sequence, then connect remote agents across processes with the A2A protocol. A modular lab you can complete end to end or one task at a time.

extra.concepts: Microsoft Agent Framework, tools, multi-agent orchestration, A2A protocol

labs.title: Getting started: set up your environment
labs.description: Shared setup for the Build multi-agent solutions with the Agent Framework lab: create a Microsoft Foundry project, get the starter code, and configure your environment. Complete this once before any task.

extra.concepts: environment setup, Microsoft Foundry project

labs.title: Task 1 – Build an agent with a tool
labs.description: Use the Microsoft Agent Framework to build a single agent that calls a custom tool: decorate a Python function with @tool, attach it to an Agent, and let agent.run() drive the tool-calling loop.

extra.concepts: Microsoft Agent Framework, tools, agents

labs.title: Task 2 – Orchestrate multiple agents in sequence
labs.description: Use the Microsoft Agent Framework to orchestrate several agents in a sequence: a summarizer, a classifier, and an action agent triage a piece of site feedback, each building on the last.

extra.concepts: Microsoft Agent Framework, multi-agent orchestration, sequential workflow

labs.title: Task 3 – Connect remote agents with A2A
labs.description: Use the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol to connect agents that run in separate processes: a routing agent discovers and delegates to a transfer-title agent and a transfer-outline agent, which collaborate to plan Caldova tech transfers.

extra.concepts: A2A protocol, remote agents, multi-agent orchestration

labs.title: Task 4 – Classify and route a support ticket

extra.concepts: Microsoft Agent Framework, structured output, classification, conditional routing
